data.narrative:
First Light Fusion, a Series C nuclear energy company founded by Nicholas Hawker and Yiannis Ventikos, has raised over $100M to date. The valuation universe comprises 11 comparable companies across nuclear energy: 3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Antares.

The stage-progression method applies directly and forms the sole quantitative anchor for this analysis. Using the $100M total raised as a proxy base value and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C to next-stage advancement, this method yields $170M. A peer-median approach was not applicable; while four same-sector peers exist in nuclear energy, none met the threshold of three or more comparables at identical stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier. Relying on all-sector medians would introduce excessive noise given the nascent and heterogeneous nature of the nuclear technology landscape.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to a single applicable method, supports a median valuation of $170M with a range of $144.5M (low) to $195.5M (high). Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 1.7x multiplier for this specific sector and stage—nuclear technology companies may follow different capital deployment and risk-adjusted return profiles than broader venture cohorts—and the absence of direct peer comparables limits calibration confidence. Additional valuation refinement would benefit from proprietary nuclear energy peer data or transaction precedents.
